Three questions, every request

Key, freshness, validation

Internet & networking · 2/4

The cache asks in this order

  1. 1Stored copy for this key? Key: URL plus Vary headers
  2. 2Fresh? lifetime > age
  3. 3Stale: If-None-Match, then 304 or 200

Internet & networking · 3/4

Directives set the answers

  1. 1no-store: never store
  2. 2no-cache: store, check first
  3. 3max-age: seconds of freshness
  4. 4s-maxage: lifetime for shared caches

Internet & networking · 4/4

HTML page versus hashed asset

HTML page

  • Cache-Control: no-cache
  • ETag, revalidate on every use

Hashed asset

  • max-age=31536000, immutable
  • New build, new URL

Pages stay current; assets never wait

Three questions decide every cached response.

The cache asks them in the same order each time.

First, is there a stored copy for this key?

Second, is it fresh?

Third, if stale, does the origin answer 304 or 200?

no-store means never store.

no-cache means store, but check first.

max-age gives seconds of freshness, and s-maxage does so for shared caches.

Give the HTML page no-cache and an ETag,

so it is never stale.

Give hashed assets a one-year max-age and immutable.
